messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: high tail latency detected in hosted inference (gpupool-4). p95 >= 950ms for 5m, p99 >= 3.1s. Streaming stalls observed. Impact: multiple customers. Paging SRE oncall. https://console.redwood.company/d/alerts/1768000001 :rotating_light:
Alisha: I'm on it, grabbing dashboards. Noted gpupool-4 as main culprit, will check node-level metrics and kube events.
Ben: seeing spike in NVMe io latency on nodes: nvme_latency p95 ~ 40ms -> 400ms on node gpu-12-3. Could be noisy IO. Also elevated context-switches and OOM kill rate?
Leila: logs show repeated GPU memory reclaim / eviction traces from our cgroup monitoring. A tenant (tenant-id: t-917) has long-running large-batch jobs. Possible noisy neighbor.
Michael: customers are reporting streaming stalls, partial token streams, and some timeouts. CS alerted 3 customers so far (enterprise accounts). Need impact classification.
Alisha: quick impact summary: p95 generation latency baseline ~120ms, current ~980ms. p99 baseline ~420ms, current ~3.2s. Streaming stall rate (stalled sessions %) jumped from 0.8% to 7.4% in last 10m.
Sanjay: on gpu-12-3 I see heavy write IO to /var/lib/redis (cache writes) and model swap churn. nvme iostat shows 90% util on nvme0n1. cgroup blkio throttle metrics spiking.
Ben: suggest immediate mitigation: 1) reduce global batching/batch_window for gpupool-4 to 10ms, 2) throttle requests from t-917 via API rate limiting, 3) cordon node gpu-12-3 and migrate pods to gpupool-6 (less loaded). Which to prioritize?
Leila: prioritize throttling tenant and reducing batching first (non-disruptive). I'll prepare a temporary rate-limit rule: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/internal/limits -d '{"tenant":"t-917","qps":5}'` (will apply to routing plane).
Alisha: Ben, can you apply batch_window change on the routing config? Command: `kubectl -n infra set env deployment/router BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10 --record`
Ben: applied BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10 to router in gpupool-4 route. Observability: p95 dropped to ~620ms after 60s. Still above SLO but improving.
Sanjay: rate-limit rule applied for tenant t-917, QPS 5. Request rate from that tenant dropped 78%. nvme util down to ~60% on gpu-12-3.
Leila: starting live migration of tenant pods off gpu-12-3: `kubectl drain gpu-12-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then recreate with nodeSelector gpupool-6.
Alisha: hold on drain for 1 minute, let's watch for regressions after batch/limit changes.
Michael: CS: informed affected customers about degraded performance and mitigation steps. Provided ETA estimate ~30-45m for stabilization.
Ben: after throttling + batch change, streaming stall rate down to 2.1%. p95 ~260ms, p99 ~980ms. Good progress.
Leila: proceeding with cautious drain now; migrating 6 pods. Expect short reconnects for streaming sessions on those pods. Notifying CS.
incident-bot: NOTE: Scheduled action: node drain initiated by Leila at 1768000250.
Sanjay: drain complete, pods rescheduled to gpupool-6. NVMe IO on gpu-12-3 falling to idle. GPU mem churn stopped.
Alisha: ok team — monitoring for full recovery. Will keep circuit breakers open for any rollback.
Ben: marking incident as mitigated for customer-facing impact. Still tracking root cause (noisy tenant causing NVMe and cgroup blkio saturation leading to streaming stalls).
Leila: follow-ups: 1) add per-tenant disk IO quotas in routing plane (short term), 2) enforce stricter pod-level blkio limits via runtime class, 3) consider dedicated MIG slices or dedicated pools for large-batch tenants.
Michael: filing customer impact notes and collecting logs for billing credits. I'll start tickets for the 3 impacted accounts.
Alisha: handing off to next oncall Ben at 1768000375. Ben: you're owner for postmortem, action items, and timeline.
Ben: acknowledged. I'll open postmortem draft and assign owners for follow-ups.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem link (draft): https://wiki.redwood.company/incidents/1768000001-potential-noisy-tenant
